stories.title: Persona 1 Remake Footage Seemingly Leaks Online
stories.summary: What appears to be gameplay footage from an unannounced Persona 1 remake has leaked online.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Persona 1 Remake Footage Seemingly Leaks Online
sources.text: What appears to be gameplay footage from an unannounced Persona 1 remake has leaked online. A little less than two minutes of video depicting what looks like a modern version of Sega and Atlus' original Persona game was first shared by a YouTube channel using the name P1REMAKE and was eventually picked up across social media platforms like Reddit . The YouTube account it's tied to was created in March 2010 and has seemingly posted just two other videos, with its previous upload published more than 14 years ago. The developers behind the RPG franchise have broached the topic of remakes for early installments in the past but never confirmed work was underway, meaning this could be our first look at the series' next remake. In the age of AI-generated fakes, you can never be too skeptical about things like this, but fans generally seem to be under the impression that the footage is authentic. While we won't share it here, you don't have to look too hard to see what everyone's talking about. Yea that Persona 1 remake leaked footage gotta be 100% real. I refuse to believe someone would do that much work to make a fake leak. There are a few reasons players suspect this to be our first glimpse at a not-so-secret Persona 1 remake from Atlus. Aside from the music, effects, and art, which all fall right in line with much of the studio's recent work, the video on display is much longer and more detailed than any fake leak would typically be. The smoking gun for many, though, is the character animations. It's specifically Eriko that people are calling out, as she seems to share a summoning animation with Persona 4 Revival 's version of Yukiko. Atlus' Persona 4 remake, of course, won't be out until February 18, 2027. There's also the issue of the appearance of Persona 2 protagonist Tatsuya, who seems to be standing in for what may be an unfinished character model. So, what can we make of all of this? Well, unfortunately, without confirmation from Sega or Atlus, not much. There is always the chance this could be an elaborate fake, with some of these odd details serving as evidence for that argument. On the other hand, it's possible placeholder assets and familiar animations are here specifically because the alleged Persona 1 remake is still very much in development. Persona 1 leak looks credible, not sure why people are reporting Tatsuya is replacing Masao, that's just complete bogus. This is most likely an internal investor pitch for remakes of Persona 1 and 2, and not actually Persona 1. There are Persona 4 Revival animations in the gameplay footage, which definitely helps the case of it being real. That sure is a persona 1 remake trailer. Why is tatsuya there We don't know when this footage would have been captured, even if it does turn out to be real. That means this could be from yesterday or years ago, with some speculating that the video we've seen today is little more than a proof-of-concept or pitch video. If the Persona: Be Your True Mind remake footage is authentic, it wouldn't be the biggest surprise to see it announced. Sega released its Persona 3 remake, Persona 3 Reload , in 2024, and will release Persona 4 Revival in just a few months. Atlus' P-Studio producer, Kazuhisa Wada, stopped short of confirming development for Persona 1 and 2 remakes in August of this year but still admitted that, as far as he's concerned, it's something "we have to do." Meanwhile, Atlus has absolutely suffered leaks before. The Persona 3 remake had in-development footage questioned by fans when it showed up online back in 2023. The upcoming Persona 6 , which, officially, we've seen little of so far, had images leak in June. A massive Steam leak in September then seemingly revealed a list of trophies – including story spoilers – for the upcoming installment. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: Rumor: Persona remake footage appears online
sources.text: A video reel showcasing what appears to be work-in-progress footage of a Revelations: Persona remake has surfaced online. The footage, a showreel similar to the one showcasing footage of Persona 3 Reload that leaked prior to its announcement, features three sections of the game—field, battle, and event scenes built around 2D illustrations. Persona 2: Innocent Sin protagonist Tatsuya Suou appears in the battle section of the footage. However, since he does not appear in Revelations: Persona , he may be a stand-in for another character. It’is also possible that remakes of Persona 2: Innocent Sin and / or Persona 2: Eternal Punishment are simultaneously in development. Other things worth noting are the constant appearance of Unreal Engine debut text in the upper-left corner of the screen and the fact that Eriko Kirishima appears to use the same Persona summon animation as Yukiko Amagi in Persona 4 Revival , lending the footage further credibility. As for the source of the footage, it was originally posted to YouTube by a user named “P1REMAKE” today at 2:25 a.m. PT / 5:25 a.m. ET . As of press time, the YouTube video remains accessible, but copies have also been hosted on file-sharing websites such as Gofile and Catbox , and shared in communities like r/GamingLeaksAndRumours . The YouTube account was created in March 2010 and has only ever posted two other videos, though its username was likely changed to “P1REMAKE” around the time the footage was posted.

sources.title: Two minutes of Persona 1 remake footage seemingly leaks online
sources.text: Two minutes of footage from an unannounced turn-based RPG recently spilled online, and yep, it very much looks like a remake of the very first Persona game. A YouTube account aptly called 'P1REMAKE' only yesterday posted a little under two minutes of footage from what appears to be a Persona 1 remake. As expected, eagle-eyed fans quickly spotted the clip and soon spread it across several other social media platforms, with the footage since appearing on Reddit and X. Of course, you should take all leaks with an unhealthily huge handful of salt no matter how convincing they look - especially in the age of generative-AI videos and such. At the same time, there are quite a few good reasons to let yourself be a little hopeful for this remake. For one, the two-minute clip is longer and more elaborate than gen-AI videos typically are. Several series fans have also pointed out the video shows Eriko summoning her Persona in combat, while using the exact same animation as Persona 4 Revival's version of bestie Yukiko. Revival doesn't actually launch until next year, which makes the pose quite suspicious. Then there's the fact that this type of leak isn't exactly new territory for Atlus' popular role-playing franchise. In 2023, footage from what ended up being called Persona 3 Reload leaked online and showed very similarly rough, clearly in-development scenes from the game's dungeons. One other curiosity is the inclusion of Tatsuya, the protagonist from Persona 2 Innocent Sin, who doesn't actually show up in the series' first game. Some folks are speculating that the video might have been created as an internal proof-of-concept pitch for Sega and Atlus management, so Tatsuya would serve as a placeholder model in that case. A Persona 1 remake isn't entirely unlikely with or without this potential leak, either. Persona series producer Kazuhisa Wada recently said remakes of the first two games are "probably eventually" happening at some point in the future. sources.title: Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online
sources.text: Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online. The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit . It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake". Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload . There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style. Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment . Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats. How do you solve a problem like Persona 4 ? At Gamescom, we sat down with series director Kazuhisa Wada to talk about the Persona 4 Remake , and ask about how Atlus is approaching the original text for the remake.

sources.text: Pre-orders open on World of Warcraft: Forever's release date Final Fantasy 14 : Evercold has received a short and swift four-week delay. Square Enix 's MMORPG expansion was originally set to release in January of next year, but an update from Final Fantasy Fan Fest Japan has revealed that it's now due to come out during the packed month of February, 2027. Final Fantasy 14 boss Naoki Yoshida - affectionately dubbed Yoshi-P by fans - revealed the news during FF14 Fan Fest Japan. Evercold's new release date is officially February 23, 2027 with an early access period beginning on February 19, 2027. Of course, February is already packed with mammoth games - everything from Fable, God of War: Laufey, Persona 4 Revival, and Metro 2039 are seemingly taking shelter from GTA 6 . Here's hoping you have a spare few dozen hours a week for all the incoming goodies. Evercold pre-orders begin on November 4, which is funnily enough the official release date of Final Fantasy 14's biggest rival: World of Warcraft Forever. ( I'm sure it's just coincidental .) Pre-order bonuses include a Kottr minion that's part of the expansion's new, fluffy, feline race, as well as a pair of earrings and early access. You can check out all the different editions over on the official website - be warned, the Final Fantasy 13 mount might tempt you to put a dent in your wallet. Evercold makes a ton of changes to the beloved, widely played online game. For one, a new Evolved system is promising to streamline ability hotbars and rejig the way jobs work. stories.summary: "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community"

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Fan-made Oblivion remake Skyblivion runs into legal trouble with a former volunteer
sources.text: "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community" Skyblivion (the fan-made Oblivion remake that's being rebuilt inside of Skyrim) has been a long time coming, but we might need to wait a while longer for the conversion mod to see the light of day due to a new legal issue. One of the ambitious project's lead modders, Rebelzize, today uploaded a video about the ongoing situation. "Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion's development departed the project. We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure," he explains in the description. "After they left the project, we had several discussions regarding the continued use and maintenance of his work. The main disagreement centered on their objection to our decompilation of parts of their work — a necessary step our team took to maintain functionality and fix issues in systems already built into the project after access to the original source code repository was revoked," Rebelzize adds. Rebelzize doesn't name the former modder in an effort to avoid creating an online "witch hunt," but they eventually sent the Skyblivion folks a series of legal threats demanding the real names and home addresses of several other volunteer team members - "something that we are simply not willing to share with somebody that we don't even know," Rebelzize says, calling the demands "disproportionate." The former modder is apparently looking to sue for damages worth upwards of €30,000. "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community that makes massive passion projects like this possible," Rebelzize continues. "To protect our volunteers from undue stress and ensure a clean break, in good faith we removed their code, rebuilding and improving the system from the ground up." Despite removing their work from Skyblivion, the anonymous former volunteer has apparently "continued to intensify their threats." The Skyblivion team is now looking for help from anyone experienced in IP and GDPR law, pointing interested folks toward their official website . Last year, it looked like a Skyblivion release date could be right around the corner . There's still no word on when we can expect the gorgeous fan-led revival, though. While a lengthy development is often filled with ups and downs, its latest woe is a rather unique one, as developers say that one of their former members is threatening litigation . “Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion âs development departed the project,” posted The Elder Scrolls Renewal Project . “We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure.” A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG — Skyblivion (@TESRSkyblivion) October 30, 2026 According to the statement, an unnamed volunteer contributor left the team a short time ago. Since leaving, there has been a great deal of contention around the work they left behind. The former developer, according to the post, objected to the “decompilation of parts of their work,” something bound to happen as other aspects are reworked and improved. In response, the disgruntled party sent a legal threat, demanding the real names of others involved. To temper the situation, the statement says they decided to remove the code and contributions in question, but despite that the former member has “continued to intensify their threats.” In a video plea , Kyle Rebel says that one anonymous community member demanding the legal names of the others is unacceptable. sources.title: Nintendo Reveals Surprise Pikmin Day Direct
sources.text: Nintendo has revealed a surprise Nintendo Direct for Pikmin Day because it has apparently decided that's a thing now. Instead of spooky game announcements or horror movie memes, video game fans woke up to on Halloween 2026 was Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto's face. That's because Nintendo has declared November 1 as Pikmin Day, and it's got a brand-new Direct to celebrate the occasion. Yes, really. None of this is a joke. There's a little more than nine minutes of announcements to go over. Although there's no Pikmin 5 reveal or anything else too groundbreaking here, Miyamoto did take the time to share new information about Pikmin 4 and promised that, "going forward, I want people to know more about Pikmin." Tomorrow is Pikmin Day! Join in on the fun by playing Pikmin games on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. https://t.co/iYxZldya7p So, to start, why is the first of November Pikmin Day? Nintendo's miniaturized franchise launched in Japan in October 2001 before coming to North America in December, so there's no tie to a release date like you might have guessed. Instead, Miyamoto explained that November 1 is Pikmin Day because there were originally only three Pikmin, which, when standing next to each other, kinda looks like "11.1." Ready to test your skills at Dandori Academy? A free demo of #Pikmin4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will be available on Nov 2. https://t.co/rNHNq35RMT You gotta give 'em credit for creativity, as Pikmin Day is probably one of the last things anyone expected to see today. Still, it served as a nice opportunity to offer an update on Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy ahead of its release November 12, 2026. Players will be able to use the new consoles built-in microphone to Oatchi, controlling them by using commands like 'rush' and 'go to work.' The Dandori Academy mode, meanwhile, comes with new challenges, including exams that take place on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, that give players timed tasks and an opportunity to earn medals. A demo for the Switch 2 version of Pikimin 4 will be available starting November 2, with save data available to transfer to the full launch. It offers access to the Sun-Speckled Terrace opening area, as well as two Dandori Academy stages. Secret Caves are coming this winter! Get ready to explore Secret Caves, face off against familiar creatures, and uncover hidden treasures along the way in @PikminBloom on your smartphone. https://t.co/Nx6Lzba6v4 Nintendo first brought its augmented-reality game, Pikmin Bloom, to smartphone devices in 2021, but five years on, and it's still got more to give. As shown in a teaser video featuring a group of the colorful plant-like creatures battling a Bulborb, an update scheduled to arrive this winter will add a new mechanic called Secret Caves. These battle-focused exploration events allow players to take their crew into caves to battle creatures and earn rewards. Before a cave is explored, players must collect a cave map, which feature information about a cave and can be found on things like Postcards. Then, Pikmin are sent into the cave to search for treasures, with some of the items highlighted during the Direct including a rubber duck, a sword, a cookie, and a chef hat. Should a battle ensue, you'll command your army by sending them in to attack when the moment is right, or retreat if things get too hairy. Pikmin 4's Dandori Academy challenges also give players an opportunity to collect maps by taking exams. If you couldn't tell from the video games, shorts , and Easter Eggs Nintendo has highlighted through the franchise's 25-year history, it's got a soft spot for Pikmin. Miyamoto has spearheaded this charge, and because he wants people to know more about the company's adorable little mascots, he's enlisted some help. Joining him during the Nintendo Direct broadcast was Japanese actress and crafty Pikmin fan Fuka Koshiba. Known for her work on TV projects like Siren and films like Lady Kaga, Miyamoto brought her in to help him "build more excitement around Pikmin going forward" after she shared hand-made Pikmin-themed hats on Instagram. "Originally, I had heard on social media that you could get hats of the Red Pikmin, Blue Pikmin, and Yellow Pikmin from those claw machines," Koshiba said, holding one of her hats. "I'm not good at the claw machines, but I really wanted the hats, so I thought, 'Well, let's just knit them.'" "I see," Miyamoto replied. "I'm also bad at the claw machines." That was a close one! Watch Hello! Pikmin short movies and enjoy new Pikmin adventures. https://t.co/8OPB48hDZr The Pikmin Day Direct also featured a brand-new Pikmin Original Short Movie. Following last year's Close to You short, this video sees a Red Pikmin do its best to grab a baseball from a frog. It's as cute as you could ever expect. As part of Nintendo's initiative to lean harder into the series, new shorts will be released monthly via the Nintendo Today! app, as well as other channels. However, there will also be a new episode released tomorrow, with another set to follow sometime in November. Miyamoto said he's collaborating with Nintendo Pictures staff to make the shorts. That's all for the Pikmin Day Direct. While there was no hint at anything like Pikmin 5, planting November 1 as an official holiday is probably a sign that Nintendo has no intention of putting a cap on Pikmin content anytime soon. While we wait for any bigger updates on the franchise, you can check out IGN's 9/10 Pikmin 4 review . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. Thus far, Funcom has focussed mainly on changes to its survival MMO Dune: Awakening , with the Norwegian studio reworking the entire game to function as both a solo experience and a PvE adventure. Now that overhaul is done, however, Funcom is now set on expanding players' adventures on Arrakis, having just announced a free expansion that adds a new and completely different map to explore. Coming in December, the Blood and Ice DLC will let players depart the searing sands of Arrakis for the planet's frozen north, adding a new survival map called the Polar Sink that flips the game's central survival concept on its head. Rather than avoiding the heat, players will actively have to seek it out, while also developing new technologies to help them adapt to the extreme change in climate. There's some variance within this environment too. The Polar Sink is composed of two different biomes, the tundra and the icecap. While the icecap is the more extreme of the two, both areas are closely guarded by "water shippers", wealthy traders who supply Arrakis' second most-valuable resource from the polar regions down to the deserts. Players' primary objective in the DLC will be breaking the water shippers' stranglehold on the ice, which they can then use to cool their base equipment back in the desert and speed up resource production. Funcom says that the expansion adds "around 35 hours of new progression", which sounds pretty beefy for a free DLC. It also apparently "brings the focus back to ground-level survival" for veteran players, "traversal, temperature management and combat all playing important roles in your progression." Blood and Ice will be released on December 1. Alongside the expansion, Funcom has also introduced a Cosmetics Store to Awakening, and is also working on several other heavily requested features. These include an offline single-player mode that's coming in November (the game can be played solo right now, but only with an Internet connection) and fully supported cross-play in January next year. Funcom also says that Blood and Ice represents "another step in the ongoing development of Dune: Awakening" and that it will "continue expanding the game" through 2027. sources.text: Funcom's survival MMO Dune: Awakening is heading north with a free expansion that trades the deserts of Arrakis for a frozen new map. The expansion, called Blood and Ice, will release on 1st December. Funcom said it adds "around 35 hours of new progression", along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialisation traits. It's coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox. The new map, called the Polar Sink, turns the game's usual survival loop upside down. Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm, upgrading your gear with resources found only in the Polar Sink. The map is split into two biomes, the tundra and the ice cap. You'll start in the tundra, where wealthy water shipper families have built lavish strongholds, before trying to get into the heavily guarded ice cap. Once you're in, you can harvest ice to cool your base equipment and speed up production. According to Funcom, the expansion "brings the focus back to ground-level survival, with traversal, temperature management, and combat all playing important roles in your progression". The studio also said future updates will add more reasons to go back to the region. Blood and Ice also brings a new Events tab to the main menu. Shortly after the expansion launches, a new event called Water Crisis will follow the current one, The Scourge. Funcom says every event can be completed in both single-player and multiplayer, and that it plans to run them more often, each with new stories and free rewards. Funcom has also launched a cosmetics store, which it says will help fund continued development and free updates. The store will start with a rotating selection of items, including looks taken from the Dune films to coincide with Dune: Part Three's release in cinemas this December. The plan is to eventually make the full catalogue available at all times. Several of the community's most-requested features are also on the way. Offline single-player is due this month, and from January 2027 you'll be able to copy characters from multiplayer servers to single-player, and from single-player to select private or self-hosted servers on PC. Full cross-play will also arrive in January 2027. "We're far from done," Funcom said, adding that it has "ambitious plans for the year ahead", including major free updates in 2027. The studio says more than a million new players have joined since the game launched on consoles, alongside a rebuilt endgame, three DLCs, and the conclusion of the game's first story arc, Book One. sources.text: An EA office building in Madrid was vandalized with the words "Save Mass Effect" just days after the company announced it had shuttered series developer BioWare. It's the latest update to an ongoing story that started when the beloved sci-fi RPG series was put on an indefinite hold earlier this month. With the studio's Mass Effect: Universe project canceled and the franchise without a future, fans have now seemingly taken their push to see the series continue with spray paint. EA's Madrid office in Spain was seemingly the target of one disgruntled fan hoping to make a change. Reddit user Ok_Link9625 shared pictures of the graffiti in question, which show at least two separate instances of Save Mass Effect being tagged around the location. "I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater and saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices #SaveMassEffect," the post said. #SaveMassEffect is an idea that emerged in the moments after EA put the franchise on hold and laid off BioWare staff, but it didn't take long for it to become more than a social media hashtag. The days following the move saw fans erect a Save Mass Effect petition , which exploded and now stands at 290,000 signatures at the time of this piece's publication. As some fans called to boycott EA products over its decision, others, like the folks at We Are Mass Effect, took their love for the series to the streets of New York. It resulted in perhaps the most famous play for #SaveMassEffect thus far, as citizens in Times Square were treated to a billboard for the movement throughout October 26. The group said it plans to fund more billboards in the near future, including one set to go up outside this year's The Game Awards. I WENT OFFLINE FOR FEW HOURS AND SOMEONE PAINTED A WHOLE GRAFFITI IN FRONT OF EA OFFICE? Graffiti, however, is a new tactic, and it has received pushback in the community. While some want to keep the pressure up not only to breathe life into the franchise but also to support the people who have made it, others have said they aren't sure how tagging office buildings will move the needle. "I'll admit, I'm not sure this is the way to make them think the IP is worth saving," another top reply argued . Mass Effect series composer, meanwhile, simply took the opportunity to recognize how quickly the campaign has evolved in just a few days: "The fans are serious as a heart attack!" We absolutely did not ask people to do this and obviously vandalism is bad, but it's insane to me that #SaveMassEffect is so big that someone in Madrid is this angry. I get it. @heleuscluster Oh shi**, man, we have banksy on our side :D https://t.co/HNHAwdFAtL At the moment, it doesn't look like billboards or graffiti have done much to convince EA to support any angle the movement hopes to achieve. The most recent information about the fallout came from Bloomberg , which reported that the publisher canned its plans to release Mass Effect 5 in favor of prioritizing Star Wars Battlefront 3 . Alleged details about the canceled game promised that BioWare was creating a story that would have accounted for all choices players made in previous installments . sources.title: Input Lag Is So Bad in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 That Players Suffer From a 'Competitive Disadvantage'
sources.text: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms. Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps. In competitive Multiplayer, Switch 2 aims for 60fps and, according to DF, hits that target most of the time (although some things do cause the frame rate to drop, including looking through the transparent visor of a riot shield). Call of Duty Multiplayer prides itself on rock solid 60fps gameplay, which provides a smooth, responsive experience for those who fuss over their K/D ratio in, for example, 6v6. It’s crucial that all platforms the game is available on offer at least 60fps to provide a level playing field for Multiplayer fans — although the debate about the advantage PC players have over console has dogged Call of Duty since the dawn of crossplay. DF reports that Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) support “helps smooth out” framerate drops on supported displays, although you’ll have a harder time of it in terms of performance playing through portable mode. And then we come to responsiveness. DF’s tests show 81ms in docked mode and 100ms in portable mode, the latter of which is double the PS5’s 49.1. In fact, DF found that Multiplayer in portable mode ranged from 83ms at best to 125ms at worst. DF called this "actually deleterious to performance.” DF seems generally happy with the Switch 2 version, which was handled by port specialist Digital Legends with support from Infinity Ward. But if you’re into Multiplayer, the inescapable fact is you are at a disadvantage. No matter how fast your trigger finger, the Switch 2 will take longer to respond. Outside of Multiplayer it’s a different story. The Campaign runs at 30fps, which was good enough for IGN’s Simon Cardy when he played the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 . “Granted, the textures are nowhere near as detailed, with flat surfaces and faces smoothed over to give the impression of plasticine versions of the campaign’s characters,” he said. “It's by no means a looker, but considering the reduced horsepower Nintendo’s latest console is working with, the gameplay itself was smooth, running at 30fps at 4K while docked.” “Yes, it's quite a visual downgrade when compared to the likes of PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X, but that comes with the territory,” he continued. “And if you’re solely a Nintendo owner who’s been locked out of Call of Duty for over a decade, you’re getting a version of Modern Warfare 4 that feels every bit as snappy as the series usually is, even if it’s a bit muddier than Nintendo’s own crisp visuals.” Why is Call of Duty releasing on a Nintendo console now, 14 years after the last time? It has to do with Microsoft’s $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Back when Microsoft was facing regulatory hurdles, one announcement designed to help convince the powers that be to green light the buyout was a 10-year commitment to bring Call of Duty to Nintendo following the merger. “Microsoft is committed to helping bring more games to more people — however they choose to play,” then Xbox boss Phil Spencer said in December 2022. Four years later, and with the Activision Blizzard buyout done and dusted, Call of Duty is on Switch 2. We’ve got an in-progress Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Walkthrough to help you through the campaign missions, plus All Collectible Note Locations , and all the Code Solutions you’ll need to open every keypad and container. For multiplayer, check out How to Level Up Fast in MW4 and our Essential Multiplayer Tips and Tricks alongside the Best MW4 Settings we recommend you use. DMZ is back, so we’ve got a handy DMZ Beginner’s Guide , too. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. sources.title: Modern Warfare 4 on Switch 2 has much worse input lag than PS5
sources.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Switch 2 has noticeably worse input lag than on PS5, which could put Nintendo players at a disadvantage in multiplayer. Digital Foundry's tech review measured multiplayer latency at 81ms when docked and an average of 100ms in portable mode, against 49ms on PS5. Testing used wireless controllers on both consoles (a Switch 2 Pro Controller and a DualSense), and portable results ranged from 83ms at best to 125ms at worst. Digital Foundry said "responsiveness here simply isn't as good as on other consoles", and described the lag in portable mode as "actually deleterious to performance" (thanks, IGN ). Beyond the lag, Digital Foundry is fairly positive about the port. Multiplayer runs at 60fps most of the time, and if your TV supports VRR, you'll notice the drops less. The campaign is capped at 30fps and resolution is dynamic. Docked with DLSS on, the game targets 900p, but Digital Foundry saw it drop to 450p in busier scenes, such as the Paris vehicle chase. In portable mode, the target is 720p, with drops to 360p. It's been 13 years since a Call of Duty game last appeared on Nintendo hardware, with Ghosts on Wii U in 2013. The series' return is the result of a 10-year deal Microsoft offered Nintendo while it sought regulatory approval for its $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Esta versão aproveita as especificações do hardware atual para oferecer resolução ampliada e adaptação nativa aos controles , preservando o design e a geometria do lançamento original. As mecânicas de trava de mira em inimigos e o uso da ocarina para manipular eventos no mundo foram mapeados para os botões modernos, garantindo fluidez na movimentação. sources.title: Com GTA 6 e Zelda, novembro começa como o mês do ‘Barbenheimer’ dos games
sources.text: Lançamentos de games em NOVEMBRO de 2026 - Calendário VOXL Além do aguardado GTA 6, novembro traz remake de Ocarina of Time e mais de 30 jogos. Confira as estreias do mês. Crédito: Voxl O ano de 2026 está bastante movimentado no mercado de games, mas novembro promete ser um dos meses mais marcantes da história recente dos videogames. De um lado, temos Grand Theft Auto 6, um dos lançamentos mais aguardados de todos os tempos e que chega após anos de expectativa e adiamentos. Do outro, a Nintendo prepara o retorno de um dos maiores clássicos da indústria: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, em um remake que promete dividir os holofotes com a aventura da Rockstar. A proximidade entre os dois lançamentos já rendeu comparações com o fenômeno “Barbenheimer”, nome dado ao encontro inesperado entre Barbie e Oppenheimer nos cinemas, em julho de 2023. Na época, os filmes de propostas completamente diferentes transformaram a disputa nas bilheterias em um evento cultural, com espectadores abraçando a ideia de assistir às duas produções. Agora, a indústria dos games tem sua própria versão dessa disputa. Enquanto GTA 6 chega em 19 de novembro, o remake de Ocarina of Time está previsto para 5 de novembro, no começo do mês, colocando duas das franquias mais importantes dos videogames em rota de colisão. No entanto, essa “disputa” pode acabar sendo mais amigável do que o esperado por um motivo importante: o mercado é gigante e os títulos estreiam em plataformas bem diferentes. A comparação com o fenômeno Barbenheimer ganhou ainda mais força depois que o programa Saturday Night Live apresentou uma esquete sobre o confronto durante o quadro Weekend Update. Na brincadeira, os protagonistas dos dois jogos, Jason e Link, aparecem conversando com o apresentador Colin Jost sobre a expectativa em torno dos lançamentos de novembro. Interpretado por Marcello Hernández, Jason representa o lado caótico de GTA 6, descrevendo um dia que envolve fuga da prisão, assalto a banco, roubo de carros e até o sequestro de um Boeing Dreamliner. Já Link, interpretado por Mikey Day, apresenta uma rotina consideravelmente mais tranquila em Hyrule, envolvendo a compra de feijões mágicos e uma música tocada na ocarina. A diferença entre os personagens resume bem a proposta da comparação. Enquanto Jason encerra sua participação prometendo “destruição, caos e sexo”, Link oferece “quebra-cabeças e combate leve” como alternativa para os jogadores. A chegada de GTA 6 tem sido um dos principais fatores de influência no calendário de lançamentos de 2026. Diversas desenvolvedoras e distribuidoras evitaram colocar seus grandes jogos na mesma janela do título da Rockstar, temendo perder espaço e atenção do público para um lançamento que deve movimentar toda a indústria. O impacto já aparece no planejamento de outras empresas. Alguns jogos tiveram suas datas alteradas para fugir da concorrência, enquanto outros projetos foram empurrados para 2027. Afinal, GTA 6 não disputa apenas vendas: o jogo também deve dominar as conversas nas redes sociais, transmissões ao vivo, vídeos e a cobertura especializada durante semanas. Confira 26 minutos de gameplay de GTA 6, que chega em 19 de novembro no PS5 e Xbox Series S/X Olhar Estendido divulgado pela Rockstar Games apresenta detalhes da jogabilidade do aguardado Grand Theft Auto VI. A Nintendo, por outro lado, parece disposta a aproveitar a proximidade com uma estratégia diferente. Em vez de tentar competir diretamente com a Rockstar no mesmo dia, a empresa posicionou Ocarina of Time duas semanas antes do lançamento de GTA 6, apostando na força de uma franquia que atravessa gerações. Com isso, a empresa pode ganhar as atenções dos seus fãs e usuários fieis antes da estreia do aguardado game da Rockstar Games. Afinal, o Switch 2 já possui mais de 23 milhões de unidades vendidas e não receberá GTA 6, abrindo caminho para o sucesso de Zelda na plataforma. O peso de GTA 6 no mercado é difícil de ignorar. O novo capítulo da franquia é apontado por relatos da indústria como o videogame mais caro já produzido e promete levar os jogadores de volta a Vice City, agora integrada ao estado fictício de Leonida. A Rockstar também confirmou que o mapa será aproximadamente duas vezes maior que o de GTA 5, com um nível maior de detalhes. O lançamento também deve ser um acontecimento comercial fora do padrão. Executivos da indústria já projetam que parte dos jogadores poderá até tirar folga do trabalho para aproveitar a estreia, algo que ajuda a dimensionar a expectativa em torno do projeto. Crédito: Estadão O remake de Ocarina of Time, por sua vez, segue outro caminho em busca de sucesso. O jogo aposta na nostalgia e na força de um dos jogos mais importantes da história da Nintendo para ganhar a atenção do público. Lançado originalmente em 1998, o título marcou época ao estabelecer referências para aventuras em três dimensões e permanece entre as experiências mais celebradas da franquia The Legend of Zelda. Agora, a nova versão conta com gráficos renovados e uma experiência mais ampla, segundo as primeiras impressões da mídia especializada, incluindo o VOXL. Enquanto algumas pessoas veem um tom de rivalidade nas redes sociais, o Barbenheimer dos games tem uma particularidade interessante: não parece existir uma disputa direta entre as propostas dos dois jogos. GTA 6 promete um mundo aberto gigantesco, violência, liberdade e uma narrativa criminal, enquanto Zelda oferece exploração, enigmas e fantasia. sources.title: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3: clássico da franquia completa 25 anos
sources.text: O jogo marcou um ponto de virada no que foi a primeira transição de plataforma da série. O retorno da trupe de skatistas contava com 13 profissionais, mas, infelizmente para nós brasileiros, Bob Burnquist ficou de fora pela primeira e única vez até Proving Ground. Isso aconteceu porque Bob havia fechado um contrato para aparecer em outro jogo, o ESPN X Games Skateboarding. A ausência do único latino abriu espaço para um dos nomes mais conhecidos dos anos 2000: Bam Margera. Publicado pela Activision (sob o selo Activision O2), o título chegou ao PlayStation, Nintendo 64, PC, Mac, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance, PlayStation 2, Xbox e GameCube. Boa parte desses lançamentos aconteceu ainda em 2001, mas algumas plataformas receberam o jogo apenas no ano seguinte. A desenvolvedora original, Neversoft, ficou responsável justamente pelas versões dos consoles mais modernas, deixando outras empresas como Shaba Games, Vicarious Visions e HotGen incumbidas das versões para PSX, GBA e GBC respectivamente. A versão do primeiro console da Sony foi portada pela Edge of Reality para o N64, já os ports feitos para PC e Mac (que foram baseados no game para PS2, Xbox e GC) foram de incumbência da Gearbox Software e da Beenox respectivamente. Outra curiosidade é que THPS3 foi oficialmente o último jogo lançado para o console de 64 bits da Nintendo (agosto de 2002), que havia sido descontinuado quatro meses antes. O game foi desenvolvido no motor gráfico RenderWare, criado em 1993 pela Criterion Games. No entanto, as versões do PlayStation e do Nintendo 64 rodavam na mesma engine de Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2, a Apocalypse. Para se ter uma idéia, a RenderWare foi utilizada até a geração do PlayStation 4, e foi usada em clássicos como a trilogia 3D do GTA (III, Vice City e San Andreas). A Neversoft começou o terceiro milênio com os dois pés na porta ao tratar do novo Tony Hawk. Aproveitando as possibilidades das plataformas mais modernas, a empresa dedicou-se a criar muitas coisas novas para a franquia. A primeira delas, que mais marcou, foi o revert. A manobra permitia que os combos continuassem quando o skatista entrava em um quarter pipe (as manobras aéreas), apertando o botão quando encostasse na rampa ao cair e então emendar em um manual. Essa novidade foi tão importante que em jogos posteriores, como Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater HD, a DLC com mapas do terceiro jogo chamava-se Revert Pack. Até mesmo o primeiro remake recente, Tony Hawk’s 1+2, continha a manobra disponível, apesar de ela ainda não existir nos originais. Outra novidade que virou um marco da série foram os Hidden Combos. Basicamente eram variações de manobras feitas durante um manual, um flip ou um grind. Essas manobras foram inspiradas especialmente nas competições de freestyle, em que Rodney Mullen dava show no final da década de 1970 e nos anos 1980. Nessas competições, Mullen usava diversas variações do manual, indo para manobras como casper, anti-casper, handstand, entre outros; tudo isso sem perder o equilíbrio e sem “resetar” a sequência. No jogo, cada variação aumenta o multiplicador de pontos do combo nos casos de manual e grind. O flip trick apenas permitia uma nova manobra (como double kickflip) que valia mais pontos e gastava um tempo maior para ser realizada. Por falar nas manobras nos corrimãos, o balanço para grind e lip tricks foi adicionado ao game. Similar ao de manual, permitia um controle melhor e mais preciso para estender combos ao conseguir equilibrar o skatista. Essa foi outra ideia que permeou para sempre os jogos da franquia, uma vez que era mais complicado de manter o equilíbrio nos jogos anteriores (o personagem ia pendendo pra um lado somente, sem mais indícios). Algumas das ideias menores implementadas foram a inserção de pedestres e NPCs nos mapas, a possibilidade de criar uma skatista feminina (em THPS 2 só era possível criar atletas masculinos) e a remoção do Big Drop, permitindo quedas de alturas imensas sem perder o combo. Por fim, a principal novidade explorada pelo marketing do jogo foi o modo online. O que hoje é comum e avaliado como básico para qualquer título, naquela época a história era outra. Afinal, o PlayStation 2 não possuía modem embutido, o que já criava uma barreira. Além disso, era a época da conexão discada, a banda larga apenas começava a dar os primeiros passos no comércio para clientes finais nos grandes mercados. Antes do lançamento do adaptador de rede do console, era possível jogar online com adaptadores ethernet USB. A versão do Xbox, ironicamente, não possuía uma forma de jogar pela internet, apesar de o console contar com modem embutido. Apesar de ter contado com várias inovações, o núcleo principal do jogo permanecia o mesmo. Afinal, time que está ganhando não se mexe, e os jogos da série até então foram muito elogiados por todos. A gameplay básica permanecia a mesma para movimentação, para a execução das manobras, o funcionamento de gaps, enfim, esses aspectos foram apenas aprimorados. A proposta do game era a mesma: fases com dois minutos para realizar dez objetivos, que podiam ser feitos em várias tentativas, e outros níveis com o campeonato valendo a medalha de ouro, que consistia em três chances de um minuto cada para obter a maior nota. As fases eram liberadas conforme objetivos iam sendo realizados, ou conquistar uma medalha de bronze ao menos. Começava com Foundry, Canada, Rio de Janeiro (torneio), Suburbia, Airport, Skater Island (torneio), Los Angeles e Tokyo (torneio). As versões da sexta geração contavam ainda com Cruise Ship (também com dez objetivos) e mais versões remasterizadas da Warehouse, Burnside e Roswell. Os skatistas são basicamente os mesmos de THPS 2, exceto pela mudança mencionada anteriormente. A versão japonesa ainda recebeu quatro novos profissionais do país. E, para seguir a tradição, o jogo contava com participações especiais: Wolverine, Darth Maul, Officer Dick, Private Carrera, Ollie the Magic Bum, Kelly Slater (que usava uma prancha de surf em vez do sk

sources.title: Tony Hawk Kicked Out Of Park While Trying To Recreate Pro Skater 3
sources.text: PlayStation 2 skateboarding Tony Hawk's Pro Skater Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4 Tony Hawk, skateboard legend, video game superstar and the last one to die in the great uprising , has inspired the culture for generations. Since Neversoft put him on the PlayStation in 1999, Hawk has been a household name, the video game series inspiring boarders on the couch and halfpipe alike. Looking to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3 , he traveled to the real world Los Angeles park recreated within the game. Only to be escorted out by security. “Happy 25th THPS3!” Posted the Birdman himself . “We got kicked out of Pershing Square while shooting this today.” Though unnamed in the game, the Los Angeles stage of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3 is clearly inspired by Pershing Square, a business park in the cityâs financial district. With its distinctive modernist features from architect Ricardo Legorreta, the stone crescent benches and large red orbs made for a slick backdrop in the 2001 extreme sports game. It still remains in the city today, largely unchanged, as well as the nearby car wash with a big blue obelisk. As such, recreating the beloved video game should have made for easy content. To the Ramones’ Blitzkrieg Bop , Hawk rolls through Pershing Square, revisiting the sights, recreating the worbling idle stance of his virtual avatar. Leaving most of the tricks to his PlayStation self, Hawk and his team could only film so much before being ejected from the site by security. “She [security] just shooâd us away,” posted Hawk. “It was very anticlimactic.” The third entry in the series was the first to hit the PlayStation 2. To this day itâs considered not just one of the best in the series, but is tied with Grand Theft Auto 3 as Metacritic’s best on the console . The game was remade in 2025, part of Iron Galaxyâs Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 bundle. While the first set was met with a ticker-tape parade, the secondâs reception was a touch milder . sources.title: Valve’s Cancelled Portal Prequel F-Stop Has Leaked
sources.text: F-Stop , Valveâs cancelled 2007 Portal prequel, has leaked onlineâand yes, itâs fully playable. If youâve heard of F-Stop , you donât need me to tell you why this is a huge deal. But if you havenât, then youâre in for quite the history lesson. In 2007, Valve spent three months on a project that Gabe Newell would later dub the Directed Design Experiments. Now, Iâm not going to attempt to tell the story better than the folks at the Half-Life wiki have before, so hereâs the short version: during these three months, Valve broke off into five teams. Each team designed and partially created a video game âexperiment,â and the fifth was dubbed â F-Stop .â F-Stop was conceptualised as a prequel to Portal , and the gameplay revolved around using an experimental Aperture Science camera to mess with perspectives and solve puzzles. Gabe Newell himself was very taken with the project, but playtesters were less thrilled. Ultimately, F-Stop was scrapped, and some of its dialogue, characters, and mechanics were reworked into Portal 2 . Well, consider it scrapped no longer, as thanks to the efforts of several leakers and the Valve Cut Content team , F-Stop is now playable in (almost) its entirety. If youâre curious as to how this leaked, the long answer is that itâs actually a combination of three separate leaks. Some of you might remember that in late August, roughly 13 terabytes of Steam depot data leaked online . The leak, dubbed Steam2, seemingly contained almost every Steam depot from 2003 to 2013 and, most surprisingly, assets for F-Stop . However, while the Steam2 leak included the majority of F-Stopâs assets, it did not include F-Stopâs source code or its mapsrc data (Valveâs folder name for its map source code data). It appears both of these final pieces of the F-Stop puzzle were leaked via the Valve Cut Content projectâs Discord server over the past 48 hours. According to the mods in the server, the person who leaked the F-Stop mapsrc initially asked for $1,000, but, for whatever reason, just ended up giving them away for free anyway. The Valve Cut Content team has verified the map files’ authenticity, and the community has combined all three of the puzzle pieces into the end result: a fully playable version of F-Stop . Those who have played it are reporting that while there appear to be a few missing assets and dialogue lines here and there, itâs essentially 99 percent complete. Unsurprising, as I’m sure Valve would have added a little more polish if they ever planned to release this officially, but hey, letâs be realââ99 percent completeâ is a hell of a lot more than the 0 percent complete we had this time last week. sources.title: Valve's long-lost prototype Portal prequel appears online after nearly 20 years
sources.text: F-Stop was a result of a post-Orange Box, 2007 Valve game jam. As reported by Kotaku , a near-mythical canceled Valve game called F-Stop has been reconstructed from material contained in separate leaks. Direct access to the build seems a little shaky at the moment, but full playthroughs of the game, like this one by Meme Man? on YouTube , are starting to pop up online. Most of F-Stop's assets came out in this August's Steam "teraleak," but the final pieces⁠—F-Stop's source code and mapsrc data⁠—were only just acquired by the Valve Cut Content Team Discord, which appears to have gone private amid all the newfound attention over F-Stop. With the Discord currently invite-only, you gotta know a guy (or know a guy who knows a guy) to play it yourself. The Half-Life Wiki has the skinny on F-Stop's origins in the "Directed Design Experiments." Following the megahit launch of the Orange Box in 2007, Gabe Newell effectively shut Valve down for a three-month game jam that produced five prototypes, F-Stop among them. It applied Team Fortress 2's cel-shaded art style to a vision of Aperture Science in its prime, all mid-century wood-paneled office optimism. F-Stop's central mechanic was a camera that could capture objects in the world, then place them elsewhere to solve puzzles. The excellent 2023 game Viewfinder would apply a similar concept to a full commercial release. But while loved internally at Valve, F-Stop's playtests were apparently more tepid. The game was shelved, though elements of its worldbuilding would appear in Portal 2 and Aperture Desk Job. It's fun to recognize some of these early ideas in the F-Stop longplays: From the jump, we get a version of Cave Johnson (sadly sans-J.K. Simmons in prototype) talking to the player, as well as the first instance of Aperture Personality Cores as companions in the puzzling. Given F-Stop's "road not taken" nature, particularly compared to the megathit Left 4 Dead and Portal 2 that would follow, I don't really mourn the fact that we never got to play its final version. sources.text: Rejoice, Nintendo Switch 2 owners with a taste for the cozy, because Hoyoverse, the studio behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail, is bringing its new intergalactic life sim Petit Planet to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. The free-to-play game is already releasing on PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, 2026, but it never hurts to have more cute and cozy content on your Switch. The news came as part of a special update on the game from Hoyoverse, which also gave us a deep dive into some of the Petit Planet neighbors you can encounter, the home decor features, and some of the mini-games available as you live your life in Starsea. You start out taking care of your own planet, but can then explore the little islands in the skies around Starsea or visit the hub-style Galactic Bazaar for things like in-game auctions and community features. Petit Planet was announced back in September 2025, and IGN got to play it a few months later , with our writer describing it as Animal Crossing meets The Little Prince. "In my short time of about five hours with a preview of the closed beta, Petit Planet offered a charming, "The Little Prince"-themed take on Animal Crossing: New Horizons with an emphasis on clear progression and multiplayer. While these are two things some seemed to crave and were left empty in ACNH, the Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail studio may offer an answer – with potential caveats." sources.text: I can already picture my late-night Leonida drives to these bangers. Grand Theft Auto's radio stations have long stood as an integral part of the series' whole vibe—either offering time capsules of the times each game was set in (Vice City), or offering a realistic blend of classic and modernity a la Grand Theft Auto 5 's excellent music curation. Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle. I've been just a tad giddy to discover what awaits me in Grand Theft Auto 6 's car stereos when the game launches on November 19, which has me surprised that Rockstar teasing six of its upcoming stations earlier this month completely flew under my radar. Well, now I've had a gander and listened to all 12 minutes of its DJs bantering and a peppering of bangers between. And I gotta say, I'm already jazzed to speed down Leonida's highways with some of these stations at full volume. Rockstar's licensed music curation rarely misses, and that very much seems to be the continuing trend with Grand Theft Auto 6. While we don't know just how many radio stations there are in total yet—this is the first game where we'll be able to tune in to both terrestrial music stations and podcasts, it being 2026 and all—but the six that were teased were the exact kind of flavours I've come to expect from the series. There's Latin station Cocoteo FM, classic country Back Country Radio, African channel AfroBANK FM, all-out metal hub The Chamber 106.6, pop banger central Flash FM, and hip-hop destination Dirty South Classics. I'm already 100% here for The Chamber's setlist, being an elder emo and all, with bands like Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer making their way onto Leonida's airwaves. But I'm also jazzed to see newer blood on the scene, like Bad Bunny's appearance on Cocoteo. My biggest interest was in Flash FM, though. Non-Stop Pop has become such an iconic radio station for me, thanks to some excellent song choices and Cara Delevigne's delightfully deadpan delivery. It doesn't seem like I'm going to be disappointed, though—Alex Consani takes up the mantle as model-turned-radio-host alongside the excellent artist Robyn (of Bulletproof fame), and hearing one of my favourite songs in MGMT's Electric Feel is all the confidence I need in Rockstar's keen ear. While the previews do show criminally little interactions between the hosts (it seems like Grand Theft Auto 6 is going for duos across all its stations, presumably for some easy back-and-forth banter), I'm sure there'll still be satire in droves to come. It has been one of the most transformative titles ever concocted, changing the face of open-world games and presenting countless hours of exploration and entertainment opportunities to an audience numbering in the hundreds of millions over the years. It wasn’t as well received, and, to be honest, I never really played it that much, even when I revisited the series as an adult. It’s a safe pick for the title of the worst GTA game ever made. Vice City Stories was one of the spin-off titles that revisited an old location with a new playable character and a fresh story, and it was pretty well delivered. It landed first on PSP as a handheld-exclusive game, but was also ported to the PlayStation 2. Some reviewers felt back then that it trumped GTA 3, which introduced the world of Liberty City, the obvious setting for this handheld title. Everything about Chinatown Wars felt unique at the time, from the art style to how it managed the open-world environment on low-end hardware. For many, this is the best GTA game ever made, and it has been brought back to life numerous times over the years via remasters, ports, and mods. It still has a pretty decent RP community backing the multiplayer platform, too. Grand Theft Auto: Vice City was a game-changer in many ways. It might seem amazing, but it came out just one year after GTA 3 landed, and it introduced an entirely new setting, story, characters, and much more. That kind of delivery cadence is utterly unheard of today, but that’s the nature of the industry, I guess. GTA: Vice City is a beloved game with a lasting legacy, and it’s one that has heavily influenced the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6. There are even throwback packs coming in GTA 6 that allow you to once again soak up the neon-drenched beauty of Vice City and get a taste of nostalgia. sources.title: Suit up as Astro Bot in Rayman Legends Retold
sources.text: After making a cameo in Astro Bot (2024), it is now Rayman’s turn to dress up as the Captain of the Bots. Rayman Legends Retold is coming to PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro on December 3, and Astro Bot’s iconic design is featured in the game as an exclusive costume, bringing the iconic platformer pairing full circle after Rayman made a cameo in Astro Bot (2024). The PS5-exclusive Astro Bot costume in Rayman Legends Retold will be available for free on players’ first visit to Victor Velour, the game’s resident tailor, at his costume shop. The outfit is once again a collaboration between Ubisoft Milan, Ubisoft Montpellier, and Team Asobi. We sat down with Guillaume Arvieu, Art and World Director on Rayman Legends Retold, and Quentin Chaillet, Lead Character Artist, to discuss the collaboration, how the costume was created, and the DNA shared by two platforming icons. Talk us through the Astro Bot skin design in Rayman Legends Retold – how did you approach capturing the essence of Astro Bot within your own art style? Chaillet: One of the biggest challenges was bringing Astro Bot’s sleek, futuristic aesthetic into Rayman’s universe. Rayman’s designs traditionally have a more handcrafted, organic feel, so introducing these glossy surfaces, metallic details, and high-tech materials was something quite different from what we’re used to. We wanted to stay as faithful as possible to Astro Bot’s iconic design while making sure it still felt authentically Rayman. That meant carefully adapting the shapes and proportions, especially his large nose, no arms / legs, and his big shoes, which are such recognizable parts of Rayman’s silhouette. The goal was to incorporate as many of Astro Bot’s signature details as possible, from the reflective metallic parts and glowing blue elements to the smooth white surfaces, without losing Rayman’s personality or expressiveness. It was a really interesting exercise in finding the right balance between two very different visual identities and making them feel like they naturally belong together. In your own words, what DNA do Astro Bot and Rayman share? Arvieu: Astro Bot has truly established itself as a major player in the platforming genre, with an identity of its own. What I particularly appreciate is how generous the game is: the richness of its worlds, the creativity of its scenarios, and the constant joy of discovering new gameplay ideas. This is something we also find in Rayman. Both games offer incredibly rich fantasy worlds, filled with diverse biomes that invite players to explore, discover, and experience a sense of wonder. They also place great importance on fluid movement, a variety of interactions, and the joy of mastering the possibilities available to the player. Beyond these similarities, I think our two franchises share, above all, the same spirit. They’re both colorful, creative games that are full of surprises and driven by positive values. They aim to evoke emotions, make people smile, and rekindle that almost instinctive sense of joy we feel when discovering a platformer bursting with ideas. These are games that make you feel good. They remind us that video games can be a wonderful source of joy, wonder, and shared experiences, whatever our age. Why do you think collaborations like this are important? Arvieu: Since the early days of video games, creators have been inspiring one another. An idea, a gameplay mechanic, a character, or an artistic approach can spark new ideas and open up unexpected possibilities. It’s an ongoing exchange that fuels our collective creativity. Collaborations like this make that exchange tangible. They allow us to celebrate the work of other teams, bring together worlds that are close to our hearts, and create moments players might never have imagined otherwise. It’s a virtuous circle: everyone brings their own perspective, ideas, and expertise to the table, and we all grow from the experience. Ultimately, it’s the players who benefit, discovering new encounters and sharing in the joy of seeing their favorite characters come together. Rayman has a long history behind him and holds a special place in the hearts of many players, particularly those who first discovered him on the original PlayStation. Astro Bot, meanwhile, celebrates this legacy while establishing its own identity with a new generation of players. Seeing these two worlds come together is therefore also a way of bringing different generations of players together. It’s a little nod to the history of video games, but also a wonderful illustration of the medium’s ability to reinvent itself and continue to surprise us. Rayman Legends Retold is coming to PS5 and PS5 Pro December 3, 2026. Embark on a bold reimagining of the beloved platformer, with new visuals and a retold story. Play solo or up to 4player couch coop, explore a mysterious new realm, jam through new musical stages, and more.

sources.text: Tackle the sun-kissed undead, uncover ancient relics, and jump aboard a train for a deckbuilding journey through Heaven, Hell and beyond. Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV – VI Remastered, Monster Train 2 form your PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for November, with all available to play from Tuesday November 3 to Monday, November 30. Let’s take a closer look at each of the games. Welcome to HELL-A. The City of Angels has been transformed into a hellish sprawl, its populace now mutated into disgusting zombies with an insatiable appetite for humans. In this extensive, visceral RPG experience you’ll journey to iconic LA locations, taking on quests, meeting eccentric survivors and enjoying a joyously pulpy narrative along the way. The game’s brutal melee combat gives you access to an expansive array of inventive zombie-slaying weaponry that lets you slice, smash and tear through the hordes before they get the chance to do the same to you. Explore the game’s expansive world alone, or practice strength in numbers in online three-player co-op to increase your chances of survival. Play the next series of Tomb Raider adventures in this remastered collection of the Darkness Trilogy, which includes Tomb Raider: The Last Revelation, Tomb Raider: Chronicles and Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness. Play with the original polygonal models or swap to the remastered graphics at any time. This single player deckbuilding roguelite sees you command clans formed of a makeshift alliance between former angels and demons, as they work together to oust powerful beings known as Titans, who have seized control of Heaven. Now, you must command these clans aboard newly forged trains, and embark on your journey through Hell, Heaven, and the Abyss, to defeat the Titans before they destroy this world. Choose from a selection of five brand new clans, each with its own unique strengths and gameplay to forge strategies fitting your personal playstyle. With three vertical levels to defend against dangerous new enemies, you’ll need to recruit powerful new units, upgrade cards, and experiment to survive. PlayStation Plus members have until Monday November 2 to add the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for October – F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896, Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 – to their library.

sources.text: New Multiplayer maps and modes, a DMZ location, and more in the first free content update. Get ready for Season 1, with new maps, modes, events and rewards across Multiplayer and DMZ. Explore the unforgiving corridors of X01, wield new weapons and attachments, acquire new Operator Skins, Weapon Blueprints, DMZ Survival Kits, and more. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 goes live on November 6 Take the fight in Multiplayer across three new maps at Season 1 launch. Brave inclement weather across the all-new war torn Backstab , where abandoned tanks litter the landscape and drone ordinance line the shelves of a deserted dwelling. Battle amidst towering rock walls in the all-new Canyon and try your luck along the River near the Convoy Ambush or take the Cliff Path for its winding pathways. Drop into a reimagined Shoot House against the rugged terrain of North Korea during a snowfall. Also, at Season 1 launch, play the fan-favorite Grind mode where you eliminate players, recover their dog tags, and take them to the Bank to score for your team. Plus, Drop Zone mode returns where teams fight to hold a single rotating objective with periodic Killstreak packages airdrop over the Drop Zone. In the Mid-Season, we drop additional new maps and modes. Battle erupts at the all-new Ministry , causing damage to an embassy as you fight in and around the building on this diplomatic summit. Overflow is the new map centered around a factory and its surrounding farmland. Counter Attack is a new mode where your focus is detonating bombs at the enemy Comm Station while protecting your own from attack. A formerly undiscovered weapons facility —codenamed X01 — has recently been seized by enemy forces. X01’s maze of tunnels and shifting hazards calls for careful planning, specialized equipment, and squad coordination. Expect new and powerful equipment and as the facility starts to close off extraction points, complete the required steps to escape, or else! In addition, expect multiple pages of new DMZ Orders inside X01 with plenty to uncover on deployment along, Threat Briefing to take down DMZ’s biggest Boss threats from Commanders and more, and Resupply Runs. Play across two new maps in Call of Duty: Warzone as the Season 1 update brings both Hajin and Zodiac with additional game modes, gameplay features, and more. More intel to arrive soon, including full roadmap covering everything coming to Call of Duty: Warzone in Season 1. Expand your arsenal of weapons with the arrival of the Cronen Osprey Assault Rifle and the CSG-35 SMG in the Season 1 Battle Pass. The Cronen Osprey combines speed with moderate power for an Assault Rifle that’s quick and reliable on the frontlines. The CSG-35 SMG excels at putting down enemies fast at close ranges as it features the highest fire rate in its class The Season 1 Battle Pass is packed with 100+ pieces of unlockable content with an all-new catch-up system that guarantees 50+ rewards for those who purchase it. In addition to the normal unlocking of Battle Pass content, players who fall behind in the premium Battle Pass will be automatically caught up to the Reward matching the current day of the season, up to day 50. In addition, the Battle Pass itself is simpler to navigate, too: Log in to collect your rewards and keep playing to unlock a linear 100-tier track filled with additional Operator Skins, Weapon Blueprints, Finishing Moves, and more.

sources.title: Phantom Blade Zero: How boss weapons transform combat and exploration
sources.text: A variety of influences come together to create intense action-RPG combat and a strange and fascinating world. Phantom Blade Zero blends influences from a variety of sources to create intense, fast-paced combat and a supernaturally infused Kungfupunk world. It draws on the tough, powerful bosses of Soulslikes, the quick, combo-focused combat of hack-and-slash games, the fascinating stories and characters of RPGs, and the unlockable exploration of search action games. All those ideas come together to create something familiar and unexpected, reworking common action-RPG elements into beautiful, fast-paced battles across a strange, devastated world. While Phantom Blade Zero’s combat evokes games like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice and Bloodborne, it takes a more hybrid approach, channeling Wuxia stories and kung-fu movies. You’re not just using R1 to dodge, holding L1 to block blows, or tapping L1 to parry them; you also need to press attack, using Square for basic attacks and Triangle for more powerful blows to create simple but effective combos and force your opponent to block and parry as well. It’s all about managing a meter measuring your Sha-Chi. Blocking attacks depletes your Sha-Chi, and if it runs out, you can be staggered and left open to attack — but perfectly parrying, and dodging and landing blows knocks down your opponent’s Sha-Chi instead, letting you cut through their defenses. You can quickly refill your Sha-Chi by pressing Left on the D-Pad to swap between your two equipped main weapons. The system pushes you to string attacks together from both weapons, or to swap as you end your strikes so you’re ready to start parrying. As you land attacks, you also earn Sha-Chi Essence. When it’s fully charged, you can unleash a Power Surge attack with L2 that overpowers your opponent, interrupts their attacks, and deals massive damage. All those elements, combined with powerful Phantom Edge weapons that have specific but limited uses, work together to turn battles into a fluid dance that constantly moves between attack and defense. And thanks to haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, you feel those clashing blades, adding intensity that shows how powerful and lethal their blows can be. One of the best parts of Phantom Blade Zero is the way it dishes out new weapons. Instead of finding swords in treasure chests or buying them from merchants, you claim most of your weapons from bosses you defeat. You get to see exactly how a weapon works as you defend against its unique capabilities, then try those capabilities yourself. For instance, after you defeat the boss Hua, Deadly Betrothed, you can claim her Scarlet Wraithblade, which summons spider lilies on the ground as you complete combos that slow down enemies and let you control the battlefield. The White Serpent and Crimson Viper are dual-wielded swords, and you can use each one’s separate combo, or mix them together for different effects that let you use one sword up close and send the other spinning in circles around you. Each weapon offers its own fighting style, special combos, and status effects, like causing enemies to bleed for extra damage or allowing you to siphon their life. With so many varied combat options, you’ll constantly want to try different weapons and see how they exploit the weaknesses of the tough bosses you’ll face. Exploration is also a big part of the experience. The game is full of side quests and stories to chase down that flesh out the Wulin, the game’s world, and the characters you meet along the way. Each area you visit is expansive, with lots of side paths and secrets to find. Often, you’ll come across areas you can’t reach yet, encouraging you to backtrack later after finding an essential item. Some paths are blocked by specific Phantom Edge weapons that you’ll earn from defeating bosses, making it possible to smash through a barrier or grapple up to a distant location. Phantom Blade Zero ties its storytelling, exploration, and combat together by rewarding you for your curiosity. Exploring new areas will often advance old side quests and uncover new ones. Discovering Blue Memory Flowers scattered throughout the world gives you glimpses into the past that unlock the stories of the places you visit. Finding all the flowers for a given story also increases Soul’s health, making him more powerful for the next battle. The Kungfupunk aesthetic informs not only how Phantom Blade Zero looks, but also the stories you find within it — it’s a dark place, constantly steeped in tragedy. Those stories lead to epic, varied boss fights against powerful martial artists and corrupted, monstrous characters. Hua, Deadly Betrothed, is an early optional boss who forces you to stay aware of your surroundings as she summons deadly spider lilies that sap your strength and stagger you, leaving you open to massive blows from her huge sword. Once you defeat her, you learn about how she was used by the man she was to marry, and her rage resulted in the massacre of the entire wedding party. Other characters represent the powers hunting Soul throughout the game, whose motivations are slowly uncovered through flashbacks as you push forward. Jing Ye, The Outlaw, comes at you on horseback and employs dirty tricks, throwing dirt in your face to obscure your vision as he tries to run you down. When you finally knock him off his mount, he comes at you with a spiked shield that damages you when you attack, and a huge sword he’ll try to bury in your flesh to absorb your blood and heal himself. And then there are characters with their own agendas, like the Gold-Masked One, a man you encounter in the strange illusory realm of the Discordance, played by actor and martial arts legend Donnie Yen. As you learn more about his shadowed story, he challenges you to vicious duels, using sword slashes, kicks, punches, and powerful, unblockable throws to rip through your life meter.
